item.description:
Sessions that keep your windows apart, input broadcast to every pane, panes that float over the others, and the scrollback kept when you quit.
## What's new since 1.4.0
- **Sessions**: Window › Sessions › New Session opens a group of windows of its own and hides your other windows, whose programs keep running. Switch to Last Session, ⌃⌘L, brings back the one you used before, its windows where you left them. Each session numbers its own windows, and its name shows in their titlebars. Sessions come back with your windows when Lokyr starts. - **Switch Session…**, ⌃⌘S, lists your sessions, your layouts and your folders: those that `[sessions] folders` names, such as `["~/src/*"]`, and the last ones where your shells worked. A folder opens a session there, or switches to the one opened there already. - **Layouts**: Save Session as Layout… writes a session's windows, tabs, splits and folders to `~/.config/lokyr/layouts/`, and the switcher opens a layout as a new session. A pane's `command` in the file runs as its shell starts. - **Broadcast Input**: Shell › Broadcast Input sends what you type to every pane of the tab, ⌥⌘I, or of the window, ⇧⌥⌘I: your keys, an input method's text and your pastes. A red ring marks each pane that takes it, a megaphone marks the tab, and a pane's context menu leaves it out or takes it back. - **Floating panes**: Shell › New Floating Pane, ⇧⌥⌘F, opens a pane over the tab's panes, which you move by its title and resize by its edges. Show or Hide Floating Panes, ⌥⌘F, hides them together, and a pane's context menu floats a pane or moves it back into the splits. - **Popups**: bind a key to `pane.popup` with a `command`, such as `lazygit`, and it runs in a floating pane in the middle of the tab, closing when the command ends well, or staying open with how it ended when it fails. - **The scrollback kept**: with `[app] restore-scrollback = true`, the panes that open again with your windows show what they showed when you quit, their colors, links and commands' marks too, then a new shell. It's off by default. - **Plugins**: the plugin API 0.1.7 reads and switches sessions, broadcasts a window's input, opens popups and reads a tab's floating panes.
## Changed
- When a pane's program ends with an error, the pane's line says that a key closes the pane, rather than the window. - The Shell menu gathers the splits into a Split submenu and the panes' other commands into a Pane submenu, and sets the tab groups' commands apart from the tabs'. - In the settings window, a key at its default shows no Reset link, the Theme Editor's Reset shows once you change a color, a key's links line up with its description, and the sidebar lists Lokyr's own sections before your plugins'.
## Fixed
- Quitting with more than 100 windows or 256 panes no longer loses every window at the next start.
## Security
- A plugin that runs Lokyr's own commands needs the capabilities of what they do, such as `workspace-write` to open or close windows, tabs and panes; the commands of the system and the integrations run of `user-commands` alone.
## Before you update
- Plugins installed for 1.4.0 keep working: the plugin API is 0.1.7, which takes 0.1.6's plugins. A plugin that runs Lokyr's own commands needs their capabilities in its manifest now, as Security tells. - Restoring the scrollback is off by default: turn it on with `[app] restore-scrollback = true`.

Commands as blocks that you can select, copy and run again, scrolling that follows your fingers pixel by pixel, and controls that look like macOS 27's.
## What's new since 1.3.0
- **Blocks**: turn on Blocks in the settings window's Plugins page, or with `[plugins.blocks] enabled = true`. Each command and its output is then a block. While you scroll through a long output, the block's prompt and command line stay pinned at the pane's top, and a click on them goes to the prompt. A thin line divides the blocks, and the gutter's bar runs along each one. - **Select a block**: click it, or press ⌘↑ for the last one, then ↑ and ↓ to move. ⌘C copies its command and output, and Escape ends the selection. - **A block's menu**: right-click a block and open Block to copy its command, its output or both, to select them, or to see Block Details: its exit status, when it started, how long it ran and its folder. Run Command Again types the command at the prompt and runs it. - **Smooth scrolling**: set `[window] smooth-scroll = true`, and the text follows your fingers on a trackpad or a Magic Mouse pixel by pixel, at every refresh of the display, and keeps gliding as you lift them. A mouse wheel's step glides, and the scroll bar's knob moves the text by pixels. - **The status bar has three sides**, start, center and end, each plugin's view at its own width. - **Controls as macOS 27's**: on-or-off settings are switches, menus of values are pop-up buttons, and the Settings, Keys and Plugins pages show their rows in rounded groups. Shortcuts show as key caps, problems as callouts, and search fields as capsules. Buttons have macOS's sizes, and a dialog's main button is filled with the accent. - **New plugins in the registry**: `sephiroth74/open-in-editor` opens a pane's scrollback, or a command's output, in your text editor, its long lines whole. `sephiroth74/git-folder` shows the focused pane's folder and its git branch in the status bar. `sephiroth74/snap` 0.3.0 makes an image of a command and its output too. Install them with `sleip add`, or from the settings window's Plugins page. - **Plugins**: a plugin can stand in for another, such as a tab bar of its own in place of Lokyr's. The plugin API 0.1.6 draws the commands' blocks, selects them, reads the command line and runs a command at the prompt. It also writes temporary files, reads a folder's git branch and a range of rows, and tells the time of day. Plugins can draw macOS 27's controls too.
## Changed
- The pane's context menu is shorter: splitting, moving and closing the pane are in its Pane submenu. - Buttons, toggles, fields and segmented controls are 24 points high, as macOS's, with rounder corners, and a disabled control dims whole. - The Settings page's on-or-off keys are switches, and its menus of values are pop-up buttons, which open over the button with the value ticked.
## Fixed
- Show Hints labels the links and paths of a long line of no spaces, such as minified JSON wrapped over more rows than the pane shows. - A text field that has the keyboard, such as the find bar's, leaves ⌥⌘ and an arrow, and ⇧⌘C, to Lokyr. - In zsh, with a plugin that switches the history as you type, the command's header no longer shows the right prompt. - A program that prints the shell's mark of a command's start, such as `cat` of a file that holds one, no longer changes the command's header nor its marks. - A plugin that starts while the view stays still sees the view at once. - A Luau plugin that hands back an empty list hands back a list, not an empty map.
## Before you update
- Plugins installed for 1.3.0 keep working: the plugin API is 0.1.6, which takes 0.1.5's plugins. - Blocks and smooth scrolling are off by default. Blocks take the command header's place while they run: move what you set in `[plugins.command-header]` to `[plugins.blocks]` to keep the header's look.

Programs that tell you what they're doing, a click that moves the shell's cursor, and tabs that keep up: pinned, grouped, reopened and stepped through in the order you used them; hints to open what's on the screen without the mouse.
## What's new since 1.2.0
- **Programs' status on their tabs**: a program that tells its state with OSC 7501 shows it on its tab exactly: at work, waiting for you, of what it asks for, done, or failed. A program's status of its session, OSC 21337, shows as a dot of its color, its text in the tab's tooltip. Desktop notifications of OSC 99 show as those of OSC 9 and 777 do. - **A click in the command line** moves the shell's cursor there, as in a text field, in zsh, bash and fish with Lokyr's shell integration, and in any shell that announces it. Backspace, Delete or a typed character over a selection of the command line takes its place. `[cursor] click-to-move` turns both off. - **⌃Tab shows the tab you used before**: keep Control down and press Tab again to go further back. ⌃⇧Tab goes the other way. `[plugins.tabs] control-tab = "order"` keeps the bar's order. - **Pinned tabs**: right-click a tab and choose Pin Tab. It stays at the start of the bar, narrow, and ⌘W doesn't close it. - **Tab groups**: right-click a tab and choose New Group with Tab to gather tabs under a name and a color. Click the group's pill to fold it; drag tabs in and out of it. Restored windows keep their pins and groups. - **Reopen a closed tab**: Shell › Reopen Closed Tab, ⇧⌘T, brings back the tab you closed last, as you left it, for 10 seconds after you close it. `[plugins.tabs] reopen-seconds` sets the time. - **Hints**: press ⇧⌘E to label every URL, path, git hash and IP address on the screen, then type a label to open it, or a capital to copy it. Add your own patterns, such as a ticket's number to its page, in the settings window's Links › Hints. - **The quick terminal from a double tap**: set `[plugins.quick-terminal] double-tap` to a modifier, then press it twice quickly, alone, from any app. - **Use Transparency**: press ⌘U to show a translucent window opaque while you read, and again to see through it. - **Text fields** have a context menu of Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All, and take macOS's Control-T, Control-P, Control-N and Control-Y. - **The settings link each key's topic** in the documentation, beside its More info. - **Plugins**: the plugin API 0.1.5 reads the tabs in the order they were used, pins, groups and reopens tabs, reads a program's status and what a waiting agent asks for, labels a decoration, and hears a modifier's double tap.
## Changed
- ⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab follow the order you used the tabs in. ⇧⌘] and ⇧⌘[ still follow the bar. - An agent's notification tells its own message, or what it asks for while it waits. - The scroll indicator of a list shows while you scroll it and fades a moment after, as macOS's scroll bars do. - The settings window's sidebar is wider, its search field and its sections lined up.
## Fixed
- The text fields take their editing keys before Lokyr's shortcuts: Shift-Command-← selects to the field's start, and Command-↑ moves the caret. - A command's mark in the gutter shows on its prompt's first line of text, not on an empty line that a prompt theme prints first. - A tab's context menu waits for a click on an item, rather than running the one under the pointer. - The blinking cursor no longer shows the character of another cell for a moment after a quick move. - A plugin whose command fails while you answer its earlier question can ask you again.
## Before you update
- Plugins installed for 1.2.0 keep working: the plugin API is 0.1.5, which takes 0.1.4's plugins. - The first time you set a modifier's double tap, macOS asks you to allow Lokyr in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Input Monitoring. Lokyr reads the modifiers alone, never what you type.
